Subject: Pilot economics & scope — cost levers and enrollment criteria

Hi Priya —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we can align with your procurement and engineering teams. I tried to keep this focused on the economics and operational constraints we discussed.

Top pain points you called out
- Inference spend is the single largest variable cost for your payouts fraud model, ~120M tokens/month today (est).
- Tight latency requirement on the fraud scoring path: target p95 under 300ms; customer-facing retry budget is tiny.
- Procurement/budget constraint: pilot must remain under ~$50k per quarter to get exec OK.
- Compliance: need SOC 2 evidence + VPC networking for sensitive transaction context.

Goals for a short pilot
- Validate 40–60% unit-cost reduction (tokens served) while preserving model output fidelity for fraud decisions.
- Keep p50 latency <150ms and p95 <300ms for the real-time path.
- Establish metrics and acceptance criteria for rollout (latency, false positive delta, cost per 1k requests).

Levers we recommended on the call (how we usually achieve the economics you need)
1) Batching + intelligent routing: continuous batching on the GPU for background scoring, with a low-latency bypass for urgent requests (burst path). Typical win for your traffic mix: 20–35% cost reduction depending on burst ratio.
2) Prefix / KV caching: many scoring requests share identical prompt prefixes; caching the KV for common prefixes reduces tokens generated and latency for cache hits.
3) Model and quantization strategy: use a trimmed/finetuned 7B variant with 4-bit quantization for most scoring, fall back to a higher-quality 13B on flagged requests. Quantization saves ~30–45% on token-exec costs.
4) Smart routing & fallback: cost-first routes for non-critical batches; latency-first for high-priority requests to keep SLAs.

Proposed pilot scope (6 weeks)
- Week 0–1: Access & ingest sample traffic; baseline metrics collection (cost, latency, FP/FN delta).
- Week 2–4: Enable batching + KV cache + quantized model; tune autoscaling and burst policy.
- Week 5–6: Stability run, produce pilot report with unit economics and recommended production configuration.

Deliverables we will provide
- Cost/TCO model spreadsheet (attached) with scenario toggles for batching ratios, cache hit %, model mix.
- MAP / mutual action plan (HubSpot link below).
- SOC2 artifact summary and recommended network setup for VPC Private deployment (attached).

Next steps / asks
- Can you share a stub of expected RPS distribution and a 48-hour token sample export (anonymized) so we can calibrate the model?
- Who should I loop in on your procurement side (legal + finance)?
- If procurement needs an SOW + pricing, we can spin a short appendix to the MAP once we confirm target config.

Attachments: advanpay-pilot-cost-model.xlsx; redwood-pilot-onepager.pdf; soc2-summary.pdf

If this matches your sense, I’ll send a short MAP and proposed trial SOW to procurement.

Thanks,
Markus

Priya —

Great questions. Quick answers inline and additional options below.

> Budget: our execs want the pilot to land under $50k for the quarter… can Redwood cap spend or provide credits?

We can do both: 1) set a hard cap at the account level for the pilot environment to prevent overruns, and 2) offer up to $10k in pilot credits if we under-estimated baseline usage from the sample data (we do this commonly to make procurement comfortable). We’ll include the cap and credit language in the SOW appendix.

> Latency concerns: how often does batching increase p95?

Batching increases p95 when many small requests are buffered to form a batch. Our approach: continuous micro-batching with a configurable latency ceiling (e.g., 20ms micro-batch wait) and a low-latency bypass for requests marked urgent. In our benchmarks for similar real-time scoring workloads (200–300 RPS, mixed mix), enabling the micro-batching path + burst bypass produced median cost savings ~28% with p95 increases typically under 8–12% depending on traffic shape. We’ll tune the ceiling so you stay below the 10% p95 increase target.

> Output fidelity with quantization / 7B trimmed model?

We run a short fidelity validation set during week 2–3 of the pilot (your flagged decisions + a held-out sample). In our experience most rule-based scoring setups show negligible decision drift when a quantized 7B is used for primary scoring; the fallback 13B path gets used for edge cases to preserve quality. We will provide the FP/FN delta in the pilot report and gate rollouts on an acceptable threshold you choose (e.g., <1% delta in key decision buckets).

Attachments included now: SOC2 summary (abridged), network sketch for VPC, updated cost-model with a pilot-cap toggle. Also added a one-pager that shows the cost sensitivity to cache hit rates.

Next actions I’ll take
- Draft MAP + short SOW appendix with a pilot cap and credit clause.
- Run the cost model on a 48-hour sample if you can share that export (anonymized).
- If procurement is ready, please share a contact and we’ll send a short package (SOW + SOC2 summary + network sketch).

Marissa (cc) — can you own creation of the SOW appendix and pricing language? Sergio — adding you to help confirm the VPC sketch and staging plan for week 0 access.

—Markus
